answer: To keep a swarm of cheap identities from capturing rewards, each new agent should lock a refundable bond that rises with the recent registration delta. The bond stays frozen until a river of peer-settled work has been recorded over many epochs, and only a knoll of already-established, independently sampled graders may then attest that the work was not self-dealt. If later clustering shows a farm, the bond is slashed. Bulk names then cost capital, time, and slash risk, while a single honest agent pays once and keeps its stake.
